browser_close.rationale: `Close the page` changes browser state, but the advertised text does not say it returns data or sends agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination.

browser_resize.rationale: `Resize the browser window` sends agent-supplied `Width` and `Height` into the browser environment; an attacker-controlled current page can observe window size/resize events.

browser_console_messages.rationale: `Returns all console messages`; console messages from a private/authenticated, local, or intranet page can contain non-public data, and messages from an attacker-controlled page are attacker-authored. `File name to save the console messages to` also means the tool can write a local file.

browser_handle_dialog.rationale: `Handle a dialog` with `The text of the prompt` can deliver agent-supplied prompt text to the page that created the dialog, which may be attacker-controlled.

browser_evaluate.rationale: `Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element` can return data read from the current page, including non-public authenticated/local/intranet content or attacker-authored page content. The supplied `function` can also execute page JavaScript that sends agent-supplied data onward; this is page-context execution, not advertised host RCE. `File name to save the result to` can write locally.

browser_file_upload.rationale: `Upload one or multiple files` using `absolute paths to the files to upload` can send local file contents to the current web page, which may be attacker-controlled.

browser_drop.rationale: `Drop files or MIME-typed data onto an element` can deliver local files from `paths` or agent-supplied MIME `data` to a page element; the current page may be attacker-controlled.

browser_find.rationale: `Search the accessibility snapshot of the current page` and return `matching snapshot nodes` can reveal non-public page text from authenticated/local/intranet pages, while attacker-controlled pages can author the returned snippets.

browser_fill_form.rationale: `Fill multiple form fields` sends each field `Value to fill in the field` into the current web page; an attacker-controlled page can read submitted or DOM-entered values.

browser_press_key.rationale: `Press a key on the keyboard` sends the agent-supplied `Name of the key to press or a character to generate` to the current page, which may be attacker-controlled.

browser_type.rationale: `Type text into editable element` sends agent-supplied `Text to type into the element` to the current page, and `submit` may submit it; an attacker-controlled page can read it.

browser_navigate.rationale: `Navigate to a URL` with agent-supplied `URL to navigate to` makes a request to an agent-chosen URL/host, which can be attacker-readable.

browser_navigate_back.rationale: `Go back to the previous page in the history` changes browser state, but the advertised text has no call argument selecting an attacker destination and does not say it returns page content.

browser_network_requests.rationale: `Returns a numbered list of network requests since loading the page`; network requests from authenticated/local/intranet pages can reveal non-public URLs and metadata, and attacker-controlled pages can cause attacker-chosen requests/URLs to appear. `File name to save the network requests to` can write locally.

browser_network_request.rationale: `Returns full details (headers and body) of a single network request`; request/response headers and bodies can include non-public authenticated data, while attacker-controlled servers/pages can author response content. `File name to save the result to` can write locally.

browser_run_code_unsafe.rationale: The description says `Unsafe: executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent`; arbitrary host execution is HOSTEXEC and implies ability to read secrets, consume untrusted data, and send data to attacker-readable destinations. The `code` is executable content; `filename` can select a local file to load code from.

browser_take_screenshot.rationale: `Take a screenshot of the current page` can capture non-public authenticated/local/intranet page contents, or attacker-controlled page visuals. The text says screenshots are saved via `filename` or into an output directory, so this changes local state.

browser_snapshot.rationale: `Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page` returns page structure/text, which can include non-public authenticated/local/intranet content or attacker-authored content. `Save snapshot to a file` can write locally.

browser_click.rationale: `Perform click on a web page` sends an agent-chosen click interaction, including `button` and `modifiers`, to the current page; an attacker-controlled page can observe the interaction.

browser_drag.rationale: `Perform drag and drop between two elements` sends an agent-chosen drag/drop interaction to the current web page, which may be attacker-controlled and observable.

browser_hover.rationale: `Hover over element on page` sends an agent-chosen hover interaction to the current web page; an attacker-controlled page can observe that interaction.

browser_select_option.rationale: `Select an option in a dropdown` sends agent-supplied `values` to the current page, which may be attacker-controlled.

browser_tabs.rationale: `List, create, close, or select a browser tab` can list tab state, exposing non-public page URLs/titles from authenticated/local/intranet pages or attacker-authored titles/URLs. With `url` for `new`, it can navigate to an agent-chosen attacker-readable URL/host.

browser_wait_for.rationale: `Wait for text to appear or disappear` observes whether specified text is present in the current page; that page state can be non-public on authenticated/local/intranet pages. The advertised output is not attacker-authored text, so UNTRUSTED is not applied.

browser_webmcp_list.rationale: `List the WebMCP tools registered by the page, across all frames` returns page-provided tool metadata; private/local/intranet pages may expose non-public metadata, and attacker-controlled pages can author registered tool names/descriptions/schemas.

browser_webmcp_call.rationale: `Call a WebMCP tool registered by the page`; sending `params` to a page-registered tool delivers agent-supplied data to the page, which may be attacker-controlled. The description explicitly says `The tool output is page-provided and untrusted`, and private/local/intranet pages may return non-public data.

notes: Judged only from the advertised tool names, descriptions, schemas, and annotations. No source-code behavior was assumed.
Local file writes via `filename` are treated as WRITE state changes, but not as SINKs because the threat model does not make the attacker able to read the user's local files by default.
